messages:
maya: Heads-up — Nightdash fired an alert at 02:12 UTC. p95 latency spiked ~2.1x and throughput dropped ~30% for the canary pool after last night's merge. stack: serving-runtime + quantize heuristics.
perf-bot: ALERT: nightdash: canary_p95_latency up 115% vs baseline, throughput -31%. traces: https://dash.redwood.ai/nightdash/alert/1725300000
sam: I saw the same, grabbing canary logs now. Early sign: kv cache eviction rate jumped and we got more kernel fallbacks to float kernels.
liam: Which merge are we correlating? I think #4523 (quantize/profile change) landed ~23:50.
maya: Yes. PR 4523 updated quantization packing for 4bit profiles; author changed some tensor layout assumptions in the allocator.
sam: Quick grep of the canary logs shows repeated OOM-ish evictions: "kv_evict: forced_eviction_count=482, active_kv_size=1.6GB, pool_capacity=1.2GB" — so working set > pool.
liam: That matches: new quantize layout increases per-shard activation by ~12% for some models (confirmed on local repro). That breaks kernel selection heuristics which assumed smaller packed sizes -> scheduler grouped larger batches and overcommitted memory.
perf-bot: CI regression: perf/throughput-nightly shows a ~25% drop in the merge candidate job for xlarge-gpu profile (job id: 987654). Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/987654/artifacts/perf.svg
maya: Can we bisect quickly on the merge? If 4523 is the culprit we should rollback the quantize layout change or pin the old packing scheme for canary models.
sam: I'm running a two-point bisect: head vs head~1 (pre-4523). Reproducing playback on canary with identical load generator.
liam: Also test switching kernel selector to conservative-mode (fall back earlier) to see if latency stabilizes — that's a lower-risk rollout fix. Command to toggle: 
```
redwoodctl rollout set --pool canary --kernel-selector conservative
```
maya: Good idea. If conservative selector reduces fallbacks and prevents overcommit we can keep the merge blocked and roll the selector change to production to buy time.
infra-bot: Prober job scheduled: prober/canary-repro-1725300200 started. Artifact upload: s3://ci-artifacts/nightdash/repro/1725300200/
sam: Bisect result: pre-4523 job passed perf baseline, post-4523 shows the spike. So PR 4523 is the likely regression.
liam: Repro notes I pushed to the run: extra logging attached. Key diff: allocation size for packed tensors increased by 9–14% depending on sequence length. Kernel selection uses estimated bytes_per_batch which is now under-estimated.
maya: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Revert 4523 on canary (and block rollout), 2) enable conservative kernel selector for canary pools, 3) create follow-up to fix estimator to account for new packing, 4) add CI perf test variant that exercises the larger packing sizes. Thoughts? :eyes:
sam: +1 to all. I'll open the revert PR and set a rollforward hold on the release.
liam: I'll draft the estimator fix and a small kernel-selector patch that considers actual measured allocation sizes from allocator telemetry.
perf-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for canary pool while triage underway. Manual ack by maya.
maya: Revert PR: https://repo.redwood.ai/r/quantize/+/4531, rolling back packing layout on canary only. Rolling back now.
infra-bot: rollback started at 02:32 UTC. deploy/4531 -> canary.
sam: After rollback (02:36) nightdash shows p95 trending back toward baseline and throughput recovered ~90% of the lost capacity. Still watching for tail blips.
liam: Will follow up with a small reproducer and perf numbers in the issue. Add test harness that simulates the larger packing (seq len 1024, batch mix).
maya: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the rollout on hold until the estimator + selector changes land and pass CI perf. Filing incident ticket: INC-2024-0677 and linking PRs/issues.
sam: Adding checklist to the ticket: repro artifact link, bisect output, revert PR, perf CI link, follow-up fix PR.
liam: One more note — let's add telemetry for measured_alloc_bytes per-kernel to make future estimator mismatches easier to catch in CI.
maya: Agreed. Closing thread once we've got green CI on the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
